evidence: STATIC: task/tests/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the frozen template tests/Dockerfile (diff empty), as are test.sh, tools/score.py and tools/restart_mcp.py. It ships every element the workbook row and quality-checks.md#22 require: (1) app runtime: Node 22 copied from node:22-bookworm-slim (line 1/4) plus `express@5.1.0` and `better-sqlite3@12.4.1` installed globally (lines 20-21) with NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules (line 9); these exactly equal solution/app/package.json dependencies and the agent image's globals (environment/Dockerfile lines 9-11), and the solution requires nothing else beyond Node built-ins. util-linux (line 13) supplies setpriv used by test.sh:110 to launch `node /app/server.js` as uid 65534. (2) Playwright MCP: `@playwright/mcp@0.0.79` (line 19), invoked as `command = "playwright-mcp"` with `--executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium` in all five judge.toml files. (3) Browser: chromium installed through that package's bundled playwright cli with --with-deps into PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and symlinked to /usr/local/bin/chromium (lines 33-38), version fixed transitively by the pinned MCP package. (4) Judge CLI: `@anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281` (line 17), matching REWARDKIT_JUDGE="claude-code" in task.toml [verifier.env] and judge="claude-code" fallbacks. (5) RewardKit: `harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7` (line 31), invoked as `rewardkit` at test.sh:207. (6) python3 3.12 from python:3.12-slim for restart_mcp.py (judge.toml command /usr/local/bin/python3) and score.py (stdlib only, uses tomllib which needs >=3.11). Tests are COPYed into the image (line 43) and test.sh does no trial-time installs. Public requirements agree: instruction.md:13 'Server dependencies are already available, so don't install packages' and integration.md:3-4 'Express and better-sqlite3 already available through NODE_PATH; use only those packages and Node', so a conforming app cannot need a package the verifier lacks. PARTIAL RUNTIME: raw-evidence-index entries (hashes verified) record scripted golden observations run 3 Oct 2026 inside image hireops-verifier:20261002-permission-repair as uid 65534 with a real restart; workspace.cjs:6 loads playwright from /usr/local/lib/node_modules/@playwright/mcp/node_modules/playwright and :181 launches executablePath '/usr/local/bin/chromium'; server.log shows '[hireops] listening on 3000' twice; workspace.json groups passed. `docker image history` of that image shows the same pinned layers (claude-code@2.1.281, playwright/mcp@0.0.79, express@5.1.0, better-sqlite3@12.4.1, rewardkit==0.1.7, the --dangerously-bypass patch, COPY . /tests); created 2026-10-01T19:03:49Z. So app launch, native better-sqlite3 load, and Chromium launch in a verifier image of this recipe are observed. RISK REASON: no full configured verifier launch/grading record exists (index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent'); rewardkit -> claude-code -> playwright-mcp/restart_mcp end-to-end was not executed, and the image used was not proven to be built from these exact frozen bytes (built from the same recipe, but /tests COPY content and build-time resolution of unpinned apt packages, floating base tags and transitive npm deps are not hash-bound). REVIEW_POLICY requires a hash-bound full verifier launch/grading record before clearance; that missing measurement stays a risk. Minor notes (template-controlled, not task defects): base images pinned by tag not digest; apt packages unpinned (NOTE-level per check-dockerfiles.py); @openai/codex and /root/.codex config are template carry-over unused by the claude-code judge; the rewardkit patch at line 41 uses assert so a rewardkit drift would fail the build loudly rather than silently. Counterexample search: a broken app cannot exploit the image (image contents are task-independent); a conforming alternative using any third-party package would fail to start, but the public brief forbids installing packages and names the two available ones, so that is not an unfair failure. An app using a Node 22 minor-version feature could theoretically differ between independently-built floating node:22 tags in the two images; no evidence of such a case and both use the same tag.
